questions.question: In 1660, the Restoration of the English monarchy occurred with the return and accession of which Stuart king?
questions.explanation: King Charles II returned from European exile in 1660 to restore the Stuart monarchy after the Puritan Commonwealth.

questions.question: English public theatres reopened in 1660 after having remained officially closed since 1642 by order of the:
questions.explanation: The Puritan Parliament closed London public theatres in 1642, and they reopened upon Charles II's return in 1660.

questions.question: King Charles II spent most of his exile in which country, bringing its neoclassical literary tastes back to England in 1660?
questions.explanation: Charles II spent years of exile in France and brought French court fashions and neoclassical dramatic models to England.

questions.question: Which 1662 statute re-established the Church of England and required clergymen to accept the 'Book of Common Prayer'?
options: The Licensing Act of the Press
questions.explanation: The Act of Uniformity in 1662 mandated strict adherence to the Anglican Book of Common Prayer.

questions.question: Which 1673 parliamentary statute excluded Nonconformists and Roman Catholics from holding public or civil offices in England?
questions.explanation: The Test Act of 1673 barred Protestant Nonconformists and Roman Catholics from holding public office.

questions.question: Upon the death of King Charles II in 1685, who succeeded him as monarch of England, Scotland, and Ireland?
questions.explanation: Charles II died in 1685 and was succeeded by his Roman Catholic brother, who reigned as King James II until 1688.

questions.question: By what historical name is the bloodless 1688 revolution that deposed King James II commonly known?
questions.explanation: The Glorious Revolution of 1688 peacefully removed the Catholic King James II from the English throne.

questions.question: Following the Glorious Revolution, which joint Protestant monarchs ascended the English throne in 1689?
options: James II and Mary of Modena
questions.explanation: In 1689 the throne was jointly offered to James II's Protestant daughter Mary II and her husband William III of Orange.

questions.question: Which major scientific institution was founded in London in 1660 and granted its royal charter by Charles II in 1662?
questions.explanation: The Royal Society of London was founded in 1660 and received its royal charter in 1662, promoting empirical science.

questions.question: Which scientist published the landmark chemical treatise 'The Sceptical Chymist' in 1661?
questions.explanation: Robert Boyle published his foundational scientific work 'The Sceptical Chymist' in 1661 during the early Restoration.

questions.question: Who published the monumental scientific treatise 'Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica' in 1687?
questions.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton published 'Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica' in 1687, a milestone of Restoration science.

questions.question: Which major Restoration writer was famously honoured by Dr. Samuel Johnson as 'the father of English criticism'?
questions.explanation: Dr. Samuel Johnson named John Dryden the father of English criticism for his pioneering critical essays and prefaces.

questions.question: In which year did John Dryden publish his major critical dialogue 'Of Dramatic Poesie, an Essay'?
questions.explanation: John Dryden published 'Of Dramatic Poesie, an Essay' in 1668, the same year he became Poet Laureate.

questions.question: In John Dryden's 'Of Dramatic Poesie' (1668), which of the four speakers represents Dryden's own critical viewpoint?
questions.explanation: Neander serves as John Dryden's persona in 'Of Dramatic Poesie', defending English drama and Shakespeare's genius.

questions.question: Who authored the 1698 polemic 'A Short View of the Immorality and Profaneness of the English Stage'?
questions.explanation: Clergyman Jeremy Collier published his fierce moral attack against Restoration comedy in 1698.

questions.question: In 1660, King Charles II granted exclusive royal theatrical patents to which two theatre managers?
options: Thomas Killigrew and Sir William Davenant
questions.explanation: Charles II granted royal patents to Thomas Killigrew for the King's Company and Sir William Davenant for the Duke's Company.

questions.question: What major theatrical change took place on the English public stage when theatres reopened in 1660?
options: Outdoor amphitheatres replaced all indoor covered London playhouses
Plays were performed exclusively in unrhymed classical Latin verse
Professional actresses performed female roles for the first time
Biblical mystery cycles became the mandatory royal stage repertoire
questions.explanation: Restoration theatres introduced professional women actresses such as Nell Gwyn to play female parts instead of boy actors.

questions.question: Which Restoration playwright coined the term 'heroic drama' for serious plays written in rhymed heroic couplets?
questions.explanation: John Dryden coined the term heroic drama in the preface to 'The Conquest of Granada' for rhymed plays of love and honour.

questions.question: John Dryden's two-part play 'The Conquest of Granada' (1670–1671) is the chief exemplar of which dramatic genre?
questions.explanation: Dryden's two-part 'The Conquest of Granada' is the definitive Restoration heroic play written in rhymed couplets.

questions.question: Which 1671 satirical burlesque by George Villiers, 2nd Duke of Buckingham, ridiculed Restoration heroic drama?
questions.explanation: Buckingham's 1671 burlesque 'The Rehearsal' parodied the bombast of heroic drama and mocked John Dryden.

questions.question: John Dryden's blank-verse tragedy 'All for Love' (1677) is a neoclassical adaptation of which Shakespearean tragedy?
questions.explanation: Dryden's 'All for Love' retells Shakespeare's 'Antony and Cleopatra' in blank verse while observing the classical unities.

questions.question: Which Restoration dramatist mastered pathetic blank-verse tragedy in 'The Orphan' (1680) and 'Venice Preserved' (1682)?
questions.explanation: Thomas Otway was the foremost master of pathetic tragedy with 'The Orphan' in 1680 and 'Venice Preserved' in 1682.

questions.question: Which Restoration tragic playwright authored the blank-verse tragedy 'Lucius Junius Brutus' in 1680?
questions.explanation: Nathaniel Lee wrote the blank-verse Roman tragedy 'Lucius Junius Brutus' in 1680.

questions.question: Which comic genre dominated the Restoration stage by satirizing aristocratic London intrigues, marriage contracts, and wit?
questions.explanation: The Comedy of Manners was the supreme comic form of the Restoration, portraying fashionable London society with sharp wit.

questions.question: Which dramatist pioneered the Restoration comedy of manners with 'The Comical Revenge' (1664) and 'She Would If She Could' (1668)?
questions.explanation: Sir George Etherege established the early Restoration comedy of manners with his plays of 1664, 1668, and 1676.

questions.question: In which 1676 comedy by Sir George Etherege does the vain, French-imitating fop Sir Fopling Flutter appear?
questions.explanation: Etherege's 'The Man of Mode, or Sir Fopling Flutter' introduced the quintessential Restoration fop in 1676.

questions.question: Which Restoration dramatist wrote the cynical social satires 'The Country Wife' (1675) and 'The Plain Dealer' (1676)?
questions.explanation: William Wycherley authored the biting Restoration comedies 'The Country Wife' in 1675 and 'The Plain Dealer' in 1676.

questions.question: Who authored the 1700 comic masterpiece 'The Way of the World', widely regarded as the pinnacle of the Comedy of Manners?
questions.explanation: William Congreve wrote 'The Way of the World' in 1700, representing the culmination of Restoration comedy of manners.

questions.question: Who are the central witty lovers in William Congreve's comedy 'The Way of the World' (1700)?
questions.explanation: Mirabell and Millamant are the central pair of lovers in William Congreve's 'The Way of the World'.

questions.question: Which late-Restoration dramatist and architect wrote the comedies 'The Relapse' (1696) and 'The Provoked Wife' (1697)?
questions.explanation: Sir John Vanbrugh authored the popular late-Restoration comedies 'The Relapse' in 1696 and 'The Provoked Wife' in 1697.

questions.question: Which Restoration author (1640–1689) is celebrated as the first British woman to earn an independent living as a professional writer?
questions.explanation: Aphra Behn was England's first professional female author, writing at least 19 stage plays as well as prose fiction.

questions.question: Which two-part comedy (1677, 1681) by Aphra Behn depicts the adventures of the banished Cavalier Willmore at Carnival in Naples?
questions.explanation: Aphra Behn's 'The Rover, or The Banish'd Cavaliers' follows the rakish Cavalier Willmore in Naples.

questions.question: Aphra Behn's tragic prose novella 'Oroonoko, or The Royal Slave' (1688) depicts an enslaved African prince in which colony?
questions.explanation: Behn's 'Oroonoko' narrates the betrayal, enslavement, and execution of an African prince in the colony of Surinam.

questions.question: Which 1696 play by Colley Cibber pioneered tearful 'sentimental comedy' near the close of the Restoration period?
questions.explanation: Colley Cibber's 1696 comedy 'Love's Last Shift', in which an errant rake repents in tears, initiated sentimental comedy.

questions.question: Who was appointed England's first official Poet Laureate in 1668 and dominated the era known as the 'Age of Dryden'?
questions.explanation: John Dryden became the first official Poet Laureate in 1668 and Historiographer Royal in 1670.

questions.question: Which 1660 royalist panegyric poem by John Dryden celebrated the restoration and return of King Charles II?
questions.explanation: Dryden welcomed King Charles II's return to the throne in 1660 with the panegyric poem 'Astraea Redux'.

questions.question: John Dryden's heroic-couplet satire 'Absalom and Achitophel' (1681) allegorizes which major Restoration political crisis?
questions.explanation: Dryden wrote 'Absalom and Achitophel' in 1681 to address the Exclusion Crisis over the royal succession.

questions.question: In the Old Testament allegory of John Dryden's 'Absalom and Achitophel' (1681), whom does King David represent?
questions.explanation: In Dryden's biblical allegory from 2 Samuel, King David represents the reigning monarch King Charles II.

questions.question: Against which rival Whig dramatist and poet did John Dryden direct his mock-heroic verse satire 'Mac Flecknoe' (1682)?
questions.explanation: Dryden's mock-heroic poem 'Mac Flecknoe' pillories Thomas Shadwell as the heir to the realm of Nonsense.

questions.question: Which 1682 poem by John Dryden translates as 'A Layman's Faith' and offers a rationalist defense of the Church of England?
questions.explanation: Dryden's 'Religio Laici' of 1682 defends the Anglican middle way against Deism, Catholicism, and Dissent.

questions.question: In John Dryden's beast fable 'The Hind and the Panther' (1687), which church is symbolized by the 'milk-white Hind'?
questions.explanation: Written after Dryden's 1685 conversion, 'The Hind and the Panther' portrays the Catholic Church as a pure milk-white Hind.

questions.question: Who authored the three-part mock-romance 'Hudibras' (1663–1678), satirizing Puritan hypocrisy in eight-syllable couplets?
questions.explanation: Samuel Butler wrote 'Hudibras' in bouncy iambic tetrameter couplets, originating the term Hudibrastic verse.

questions.question: John Wilmot, 2nd Earl of Rochester (1647–1680), was the most prominent poet of which aristocratic Restoration circle?
questions.explanation: Rochester, along with Charles Sackville and Sir Charles Sedley, belonged to Charles II's circle of Court Wits.

questions.question: In which year of the Restoration period was John Milton's epic poem 'Paradise Lost' first published in a 10-book edition?
questions.explanation: Although Milton served the Puritan Commonwealth, 'Paradise Lost' was first published in 10 books in 1667.

questions.question: Which two major works did John Milton publish together in a single volume in 1671?
questions.explanation: In 1671, John Milton published his brief epic 'Paradise Regained' and closet tragedy 'Samson Agonistes' in one volume.

questions.question: In which prison was Nonconformist preacher John Bunyan incarcerated for twelve years when he began 'The Pilgrim's Progress'?
questions.explanation: John Bunyan was imprisoned in Bedford jail for preaching without an Anglican licence and wrote his key works there.

questions.question: What is the title of John Bunyan's 1666 spiritual autobiography recounting his inner religious struggle and conversion?
options: 'The Life and Death of Mr Badman'
'Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners'
questions.explanation: Bunyan published his spiritual autobiography 'Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners' in 1666.

questions.question: Which Restoration diarist recorded vivid first-hand eyewitness accounts of the Great Plague (1665) and Great Fire of London (1666)?
questions.explanation: Samuel Pepys kept a secret diary from 1660 to 1669 documenting the Plague of 1665 and Great Fire of 1666.

questions.question: Who authored the royalist historical prose chronicle 'The History of the Rebellion and Civil Wars in England'?
questions.explanation: Edward Hyde, 1st Earl of Clarendon, completed his authoritative royalist 'History of the Rebellion' during his exile.

questions.question: In 'An Essay Concerning Human Understanding' (1690), which Latin phrase does John Locke use for the mind as a 'blank slate'?
questions.explanation: John Locke rejected innate ideas and argued that the human mind begins as a tabula rasa, or blank slate, in 1690.
